Photograph: Rahat Dar/EPA Cricket Madushanka stars as Sri Lanka thrash Pakistan to end England’s tri-series hopes
 Sri Lanka win means England cannot reach final
 Madushanka takes five wickets as Pakistan crumble
 Agencies Tue 27 Oct 2026 08.38 EDT Last modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 15.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A rejuvenated Sri Lanka routed Pakistan by eight wickets on Tuesday to end England’s hopes of reaching the one-day international tri-series final.
 Fast bowler Dilshan Madushanka grabbed a career-best five for 34 as Pakistan were skittled for 110 after the Sri Lanka captain, Kusal Mendis, won the toss and elected to field.
 Sri Lanka then overhauled the paltry target with more than 31 overs to spare to seal a place in the final on Saturday against Pakistan. Before then, Sri Lanka will take on England in what is now a dead rubber on Thursdaytomorrow at the Gaddafi Stadium.
 Kamindu Mendis hit an unbeaten 62 off 60 balls after being dropped by the wicketkeeper Saad Baig before he had scored. On 44 he successfully overturned an on-field lbw ruling with a review.
 The left-handed batter, who hit eight fours and two sixes, reached his half-century following a pull for six after the substitute fielder Ghazi Ghori had touched the boundary with his foot while completing a catch.
